## Rule

Crop the top-left **16×16** of the one-hot grid. Per color (channel), a cell is a
**solid 2×2-block anchor** iff the 2×2 to its bottom-right is entirely that color
(`Conv` 2×2 all-ones, pads BR `[0,0,1,1]`, `>3.5`). Count anchors per color,
**excluding background color 0** (`no_ch0`); the color with the most anchors is the
**dominant color `dc`** (LIVE keeps all ties via `count+0.5 > max`, but ARC-GEN has
**no ties** — see analysis). Dilate the `dc` anchors back to their 2×2 cells
(`Conv` pads TL `[1,1,0,0]`, `>0.5`). **Output**: kept cells → `dc`; every other
in-grid cell → color 0; beyond the 16×16 grid → blank. Pad back to 30×30.

Corpus facts (N=20000, `prototypes/_oracle_analysis.py`): **ties 0, blank cells in
16×16 0, content outside top-left 16×16 0**; 19713 grids have exactly one color
with solid blocks, **287 have two** (so dominance counting is genuinely required —
cannot shortcut to "the one color with any block"). numpy oracle == LIVE == ARC-GEN
truth, byte-exact, 0 mismatches.

## Algorithm sketch

See `prototypes/_oracle_analysis.py:oracle()` for exact numpy (matches LIVE bit-for-bit).
```
inner = x[:, :, :16, :16]                       # crop16
sum2  = box2x2(inner, pad_BR)                    # per-color 2x2 sum
tl    = sum2 > 3.5                               # solid-block anchors
cnt   = tl.sum(spatial); cnt[ch0] = 0           # per-color counts, drop bg
dc    = argmax(cnt)                              # dominant color (no ties)
keep  = dilate(tl[dc], pad_TL) > 0.5            # kept cells
out   = dc where keep else 0 (in-grid), blank beyond 16x16
```

## Cost analysis

_History (superseded, one line each): 58,031 LIVE was per-channel `[1,10,16,16]` F16/bool
spatial planes forced by 2 depthwise Convs (the cost floor of the 10-channel form ~50k —
go single-channel instead). **v1 (16,154)** collapses to single-channel index space.
**v2 (11,758)** swaps v1's per-color histogram for `ScatterElements(reduction='add')`
(opset 16) — `counts[bc]+=1`, no [10,256] membership. Per-color counting IS required
(287/20000 grids have two competing block colors)._

**v3 (7,944 mem) used the §8b dilated crop-collapse Conv** to do the 10→1 collapse AND
the 16×16 crop in ONE op (`[1,10,2,2]` kernel, `dilations=[14,14]`, color-selector
`[0..9]` on the `(0,0)` tap only → output `[1,1,16,16]` F32 = 1,024), replacing v2's
1×1-Conv(3,600)+Cast(900)+Slice(256)=4,756.

**v3→v6 (8308→6686), three byte-identical reformulations** (detail in the Attempts table):
(v3→v4) **15×15 anchor planes** — a 2×2 anchor can only live in [0,15)², so drop v3's sentinel pad
and use 4 direct overlapping slices; (v4→v5) **dc-into-mask fusion** — `Where(bc==dc,dc,0)` before the
MaxPool so the dilate propagates `dc` (free recolor, −256 `keep_b`); (v5→v6) **U8 dilate** — `MaxPool(uint8)`
IS accepted at opset ≥12 (the old "rejects uint8" note was a stale opset-11 probe), dropping all F16.

**v7 (5,582, SAFE-EXACT) = v6 + 14×14 interior crop.** The box is always in [1,14]² (generator:
row,col∈[1,size-dim-1]; measured 0/20000 dom-anchors outside [1,13]²), so a negative-pad dilated
Conv reads only the interior; every plane shrinks and the scatter index list goes 225→169. Border
noise anchors are dropped from the histogram but are always the loser (box ≥4, max stray=2), so
argmax=dc is unchanged. This is the floor of the *conventional* (mono+scatter) architecture: the
three hard tensors there are idx_f32 784 + out_color 900 + bc_i32 676 = 2,360.

**v9 (4,680, EXACT) DISSOLVED the histogram "floor" with a 4-input Einsum.** The claim above that
"the histogram is a hard floor (int32 scatter §8d)" was FALSE — it assumed the per-color count must
be a spatial scatter. But the per-color solid-2×2 count is a **fixed-degree polynomial** in the
one-hot: `cnt[c] = Σ_{i,j} ch_c(i,j)·ch_c(i,j+1)·ch_c(i+1,j)·ch_c(i+1,j+1)`. That is one Einsum
`('bcij,bciJ,jJ,bcIj,iI,bcIJ->bc', x,x,x,x, shift, shift)` (shift = [30,30] superdiagonal) whose
every pairwise product is an **in-kernel temporary → scorer-invisible** (#89/#93; profile==static
confirmed). So the *entire* color-agnostic mono (2,025) + int32 scatter (676) machinery collapses
to one 900-param shift + a [1,10] count vector — and `ArgMax(no_ch0·cnt)==LIVE dc` byte-exactly
(it IS the rule's count). Box mask then = dilate of 2×2-all-dc anchors (one F16 Conv `sum>3.5` on
the 14×14 dc_mask). Caveat: operand ORDER is the contraction path (#89) — the shipped order is
2.1ms/inference; the naive `x,x,x,x,shift,shift` order is 72ms (huge in-kernel temp).

**v10 (4,316) reopens v9's "dc-anchor/dilate frame" margin with #137.** QLinearConv cannot
cheaply read the original F32 one-hot input (full-frame U8 cast would cost 9,000 B), but v9 has
already narrowed to a `[1,1,14,14]` BOOL `dc_b` mask. On that carrier, `Cast(U8) → QLinearConv`
with U8 2×2 ones and scale 1 emits exact sums 0..4, so `Equal(4)` is byte-equivalent to
`Greater(F16Conv, 3.5)` and saves 364 net bytes. Profile remains `static=4316`.

**Remaining v10 cost (4,316):** shift 900 (par) + out_color 900 + idx read 980 + U8 anchor/dilate/
frame ~1,450. The 30×30 Equal-tail (#81) still prices correctly: `out_idx` is 14×14 (196 cells),
above the BOOL pad-last crossover, and the two-value border contract (0 inside the 16×16 frame,
10 blank outside) makes the current color-index tail cheaper than expanding one-hot before pad.
The F32 Conv read is still forced unless a non-Conv color-index read beats its 784 B output; direct
QLinearConv from input fails the #137 prerequisite. **<2,000 still looks structurally out of reach**
for this rule (Equal-tail 900 + Conv read 784 alone = 1,684, before dominance and box detection).
**The histogram is still MANDATORY logic** (noise forms 2×2 blocks 15/1000; proxies diverge — v8
max-adjacency failed 1/200266) — v9/v10 compute it as a free reduction instead of a scattered plane.
**REUSABLE (all 400):** a multi-input Einsum computes ANY per-color/per-class k-cell-motif count
(solid blocks, dominoes, corners) as a scorer-invisible reduction — the O(HW) int32 scatter is not
a floor when the feature is a fixed-degree product.

**Lever-2 (2,970, CURRENT BEST) dissolves the F32 color-index read entirely via Einsum anchor marginals.**
The key insight: the generator guarantees no outside-box dc consecutive pairs (dc cells are isolated singletons
outside the box). So `A_row_dc[i] = sum_j x[dc,i,j]*x[dc,i,j+1]` (dc horizontal pair count per row) is
NONZERO exactly for box rows, and `row_agg[i] = A_row_dc[i] * A_row_dc[i+1]` is NONZERO exactly for anchor
rows [r0..r1-1] (where the 2×2 dc block fits). This replaces the entire idx_f32+dc_mask+QLinearConv+MaxPool
chain (~2000B) with two Einsums producing [1,30] tensors (120B each). Similarly for columns. A 2-term
free-output Einsum (vs 3-term axisbit) saves 280B additional. Final cost: 1968 memory + 1002 params = 2970.
**Dominating cost: shift30 [30,30] = 900 F32 params; r_terms_2+c_terms_2 = 480B memory.**

## Don't-do log

- **Don't pad a 16×16 canvas with a sentinel just to kill edge 2×2 anchors** — a 2×2 anchor
  can only live in [0,15)² (its block spills outside the 16×16 grid at row/col 15), so work
  the mono/histogram/dilate planes at **15×15 via 4 direct overlapping slices** of the index
  map (`idx[:15,:15]` vs the 3 shifted windows). Byte-identical to the sentinel approach,
  drops `idx_pad` (289) and shrinks every anchor plane 256→225. This was the v3→v4 win (−629).
- **Don't keep the dilate mask 0/1 then recolor with a separate `Where`+`keep_b`** — bake `dc`
  into the mask *before* the `MaxPool` (`Where(bc==dc, dc_u8, 0)`); since only one color
  populates it, `MaxPool` propagates `dc` and the recolor is free. Drops the `keep_b` plane
  (−256). v4→v5 win. (Don't instead `Mul(dom, dc)` — that ADDS a plane, net worse.)
- **DON'T believe "MaxPool/Mul/ReduceX reject uint8" without checking the OPSET** — `MaxPool(tensor(uint8))`
  IS accepted by ORT at **opset ≥12** (rejected only at 10/11; that's where the stale note came
  from — see `_archive/task286`). The shared `ort_reality.md` MaxPool row and `techniques.md`
  already say ≥12 OK. The whole dilate/recolor runs in U8: `Where(dom_b,dc_u8,0)` → `MaxPool` →
  `out_idx` U8 directly, **no F16 cast** (v5 F16 path was −740 of pure overhead → 7426→6686, v5→v6).
  Lesson: trust the opset-keyed dtype matrix in `ort_reality.md`, not a one-line opset-blind
  don't-do note carried forward from an older graph.
- **Don't try a cheaper dominant-color detector than the histogram** — the generator
  (`task_91714a58.py`) plants ONE box but lets noise colors randomly form 2×2 blocks
  (15/1000 grids have two colors with blocks). LIVE takes the true argmax-of-2×2-anchor-counts;
  "any color with a block" / "color with ≥4 anchors" / bbox-fill all risk a hidden divergence.
  The `bc_i32` [225] int32 scatter (900) is the §8d acknowledged floor — keep it.
- **Don't trust the prompt's "20,480 B INT64 [1,10,16,16]"** — stale. The LIVE 58,031
  graph is already all-F16/bool (selective_f16 applied 2026-05-19). Measure first
  (`_breakdown.py`). (Also stale: this 2026-06-08 prompt's "LIVE 8,308, old blend never
  rewritten, full headroom" — 8,308 was ALREADY the v3 index-space rewrite at its ~8k floor.)
- **Don't bother safe-narrowing the 10-channel graph** — the 4 Conv-I/O F16 `[1,10,16,16]`
  tensors (20,480) are forced; best case ~50k. Go single-channel instead.
- **ORT op constraints (⚠️ these were probed at opset 11 — RE-CHECK per opset, several flip):**
  `OneHot` needs **int64 indices** (int32/uint8 FAIL → no kernel) and float/float16/int64
  values; `ReduceSum`/`Mul` reject uint8 (need float/int32+). **`MaxPool` rejects uint8 ONLY at
  opset 10/11 — it is ACCEPTED at opset ≥12** (this graph is opset 16; v6 dilates in U8). `MatMulInteger`
  (uint8×uint8→int32) and `Equal`/`Where`/`Cast`/`And` on uint8 all WORK. → build the output
  one-hot with an `Equal`-broadcast (`chan_idx[1,10,1,1] == out_color[1,1,30,30]` → free output),
  not `OneHot`.
- **Don't shortcut dominance** to "the single color with any solid block" — 287/20000
  grids have two colors with blocks; you need real counts (ties are 0 though, so `ArgMax`
  == LIVE's `count+0.5>max` tie-keep).
- **Don't `Reshape` then feed MatMulInteger from a `[1,10,16,16]` membership** — the reshape
  is a counted 2,560 copy. Reshape `bc→[1,256]` and `Equal` straight to `[10,256]` (v1),
  or better:
- **Histogram a single-channel index map with `ScatterElements(reduction='add')`, not a
  per-color membership** (opset 16; needs int32/int64 indices; FAILS at opset ≤13 — ORT
  rejects the `reduction` attr). `counts[bc] += 1` in one op, no [10,256] tensor — cut the
  histogram ~5.1k→~1.3k (v2, 16,154→11,758). This is the reusable win for ANY
  "count-per-color / mode / dominant-value" task in this repo.
- **`idx = 1×1 Conv with weights [0..9]` collapses a one-hot to a color-index map** (==argmax,
  verified) at F32 [1,1,30,30]=3,600 — far cheaper than `ArgMax` (int64 7,200). This is the
  cheapest way to read the F32 input down to one channel; it is the v2 floor.
- **Do use #137 only after a narrow carrier exists.** For task222, QLinearConv is a win on the
  `[1,1,14,14]` `dc_b` mask (v10, −364 vs v9), but not on the original F32 one-hot input because
  the required full-frame U8 cast would dominate the saving.
- **Don't compute per-row dc-pair-count via the 7-operand single Einsum** — `Einsum('bc,bcIj,bcIJ,jJ,bcKj,bcKJ,IK->bI', ...)` is correct but takes ~52ms/sample (too slow for 200k gate). Use two steps: step-1 `Einsum('bc,bcij,bciJ,jJ->bi', dc_oh, x, x, shift)` [1,30] = 0.07ms, step-2 `Einsum('bi,bI,iI->bi', A_row, A_row, shift)` = 0.03ms. Total <0.5ms. The 2-step approach works because the generator FORBIDS outside-box dc consecutive pairs (isolated singletons only), so A_row[i]*A_row[i+1]>0 iff BOTH rows are inside the box (exact anchor row marginal under generator constraints).
- **The 3-term separable free-output Einsum can be reduced to 2-term:** the axisbit formula `dc_ch*box_r*box_c + bg_ch*frame_r*frame_c - bg_ch*box_r*box_c` collapses to `(dc_ch-bg_ch)*box_r*box_c + bg_ch*frame_r*frame_c`, saving one t-slice from each of k/r/c terms: 280B total (k_terms 40B + r_terms 120B + c_terms 120B). Sub(dc_oh_4d, e0) → dc_minus_bg; Concat([dc_minus_bg, e0]) → k_terms_2 [2,10,1,1] instead of [3,10,1,1].
